investigation.name: Demo · real case: United States v. Anise (cash structuring)
investigation.question: Did Magdy Anise split cash into deposits under $10,000 across five bank accounts to avoid the banks' reports, and how much?
investigation.description: A demo built from one public record: the 2015 federal grand jury indictment of New Jersey attorney Magdy Fouad Anise (D.N.J., Crim. No. 2:15-cr-00218), which lists 144 dated cash deposits into five accounts in his name between December 2009 and January 2012. Everything here is an allegation in the indictment, quoted exactly; the record does not say how the case ended. Loaded to show the structuring red flag (ML-021) on real data.

claims.text: Anise made cash deposits just under $10,000 into five accounts in his name to keep his banks from filing currency transaction reports.
claims.rationale: Charged in a grand jury indictment; an indictment is an allegation, and this record does not say how the case ended.

evidence.quote: by breaking down amounts of United States currency into amounts of less than $10,000 prior to depositing such currency with said financial institutions
including the following structured deposits into two Banco Popular accounts, two JP Morgan accounts, and one Bank of America account in the name of defendant ANISE

claims.text: After JP Morgan's April 2010 letter, Anise stopped structuring deposits into the JP Morgan account ending in 6100 but kept doing so at Banco Popular 0979, JP Morgan 3770 and Bank of America 2315.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the indictment; the deposit table shows no JP Morgan 6100 deposits after the letter.

evidence.quote: After defendant ANISE received the letter, he ceased structuring cash deposits into the JP Morgan account ending in 6100, but continued to structure cash
deposits into the Banco Popular account ending in 0979, the JP Morgan account ending in 3770, and the Bank of America account ending in 2315.

claims.text: The money Anise deposited came in part from cash kickbacks doctors paid him for referring personal-injury clients.
claims.rationale: Alleged in the indictment; the deposit table itself does not say where each deposit's cash came from.

evidence.quote: From in or about 2009 through in or about 2012, defendant ANISE accumulated approximately $800,000 in cash, including cash from the kickback scheme mentioned above.
From in or about 2009 through in or about 2011, defendant ANISE received cash kickbacks from doctors and others in exchange for ref erring his personal-injury clients to them.
